image_description: A close-up, underwater shot of a grey whale's head and rostrum. The image highlights the textured, mottled grey skin covered in barnacles (callosities) and cyamids. The arched upper jaw and lower jaw are visible, with a glimpse of the baleen plates inside the mouth on the left side. The background is murky green water.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight close-up of the snout/mouth area; the top of the head where blowholes are located is outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture clearly shows the characteristic mottling and raised white/grey barnacle clusters typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal region is not visible in this head-focused crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: On the left edge of the open mouth, vertical cream-colored structures consistent with baleen plates are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are not visible in this frame.

Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: High-resolution detail confirms the rough, bumpy texture associated with callosities and barnacles.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness/blurring at the very edge of the lower jaw where it meets the water, potentially indicating minor generation smoothing or focus fall-off, but largely consistent with underwater photography physics.

The baleen plates lack distinct individual separation in the deeper parts of the mouth, appearing somewhat fused or muddy, which is a common AI struggle with repetitive fine structures, though plausible due to lighting/turbidity.
